tools.name: bb_search
tools.description: Unified indexed retrieval for symbol lists, content, exact symbol source, or files. This is retrieval, not natural-language explanation or code analysis. Symbol/content/file modes carry a freshness block ({ fresh, stale, missing, staleRatio, mode, remediation }) stating whether results reflect the current files; rows may carry stale=true. Remediation names the exact reindex command. When a read finds stale/missing files within budget, the handler auto-refreshes exactly those files (reindexFilesParallel) before answering and declares it in an autoRefresh field; refresh=false opts out and answers from existing data with the staleness block.

query.description: symbol/content query; also accepted as the exact symbol name

symbolName.description: exact symbol name for symbol mode

language.description: filter by language (e.g. typescript, python, go)

symbolKind.description: filter by symbol kind (function, class, variable, interface, enum, ...)

includeContent.description: include a code snippet per result (default false)

regex.description: treat query as a regex against symbol names (default false)

refresh.description: false opts out of the inline auto-refresh of stale files (default: auto-refresh within budget before answering)

documentation.summary: Unified lexical, content, exact-symbol, and file retrieval.

returns: Indexed matches with file and line provenance
Exact symbol or bounded file source in retrieval modes
Freshness state where available
errors: Missing mode-specific query, symbolName, or filePath
limitations: Results reflect the current index and may be stale
Content search is lexical; use bb_ask for semantic discovery
tools.performance: Pagination and result limits bound retrieval; exact indexed lookup is preferred over content scanning.
tools.safety: Read-only. It does not refresh the index or modify source files.
tools.evidence: Paths, line ranges, symbol kinds, and source snippets are indexed evidence; stale flags qualify that evidence.

tools.name: bb_ask
tools.description: Answer a question about the codebase using semantic search over the index. Returns matched symbols with similarity scores.
returns: Natural-language answer
Ranked semantic matches
Similarity and source provenance
limitations: Semantic similarity discovers candidates but does not independently prove a claim
Local word vectors provide lexical-quality fallback rather than model-quality semantics
tools.performance: The limit bounds returned semantic matches; embedding coverage and model choice affect ranking quality.
tools.safety: Read-only. It does not write source or silently rebuild embeddings.
tools.evidence: Treat matched symbols and resolvable source locations as evidence; treat generated explanation as interpretation.

tools.name: bb_health
tools.description: Unified index health: file/symbol/relationship/imports counts, embedding model + coverage, schema version, runtime, and file freshness. Use verbose=true for per-language breakdown and stale-file names, refresh=true to reindex before reporting, force=true to force a full in-place reindex before reporting, integrity=true for the 12-point index health check, complete=true for full (not sampled) freshness, includeAnalysisRuns=true for persisted run/finding totals, history=true for persisted analysis history.

force.description: force a full in-place reindex before reporting

wait.description: wait for refresh to finish (default true)

documentation.summary: Unified index, schema, freshness, embeddings, runtime, integrity, and analysis history.

returns: Index, schema, runtime, freshness, and embedding health
Optional integrity and analysis-history summaries
Typed warnings and refresh outcome
limitations: Sampled freshness is not a complete filesystem proof
Embedding coverage reports stored state, not semantic quality
tools.performance: Sampled freshness is the default; complete freshness and integrity checks intentionally cost more.
tools.safety: Status is read-only. refresh=true explicitly mutates only index data; force=true performs a full in-place reindex.
tools.evidence: Counts and versions come from the brain database; freshness compares indexed metadata with the filesystem.

tools.name: bb_patterns
tools.description: Detect orphaned code, framework patterns, and anti-patterns, with staleness markers when a finding's file changed after indexing. Use scope=orphaned for dead code; scope=all (default) for the full pattern scan with the optional pattern/confidence filters. Architecture and code-quality analysis are planned, not yet executable.

scope.description: orphaned only, or all pattern classes (default all)

includeOrphaned.description: include orphaned-code patterns in an all scan (default true)

recordRun.description: persist this scan as an analysis run

documentation.summary: Pattern/orphan analysis with optional persisted run history.

returns: Pattern findings with confidence and locations
Orphan, framework, and anti-pattern classifications
Optional persisted run history
limitations: Orphan status is static incoming-reference evidence, not proof that code is unused
Framework and anti-pattern detection is heuristic and confidence-qualified

Candidates are derived from analyzer-extracted symbols and relationships; the same graph gaps (dynamic/reflection wiring, unresolved cross-file references) that limit the analyzers also constrain these detections
tools.performance: The result limit and confidence threshold bound reporting; history access is separately limited.
tools.safety: Source is read-only. recordRun writes only analysis-history records in the brain database.
tools.evidence: Every finding is confidence-qualified and tied to indexed files, symbols, or relationships.

tools.name: bb_security
tools.description: Cross-language security scan: SQL injection, XSS, command injection, hardcoded secrets, weak crypto. Findings whose underlying file changed after indexing carry a staleness marker.

recordRun.description: persist this scan as an analysis run

documentation.summary: Cross-language findings with optional persisted run history.

returns: Normalized security findings
Cross-language source-to-sink flow evidence
Optional persisted run history
limitations: Static taint analysis can produce false positives and false negatives
It is not runtime testing or a penetration test
tools.performance: Indexed flow analysis and output/history limits bound work and response size.
tools.safety: Source is read-only. recordRun writes only analysis-history records in the brain database.
tools.evidence: A finding is supported by indexed source/sink locations and relationship paths; severity does not imply exploitability.

tools.name: bb_visualize
tools.description: Scoped dependency and architecture visualization over the canonical graph engine, with explicit filters, provenance, truncation, machine-readable JSON, and self-contained HTML. Every node and link carries a stale flag (file changed since index); links inherit worst-of-endpoints; a freshness envelope rides the JSON output. Same owner-cascade semantics as bb_graph: member-level relationships are attributed to the owner class.

target.description: file, module, symbol, or feature target (`symbol`/`symbolName`/`query` are accepted as aliases)

documentation.summary: Scoped canonical dependency graphs with explicit truncation and provenance.

returns: Canonical nodes and links
Text, JSON, or self-contained HTML projection
Provenance and explicit truncation metadata
errors: Missing target for a scoped graph
limitations: The graph reflects static indexed relationships
Nodes and links beyond configured budgets are omitted and reported
Owner-cascade attribution: member-level relationships are attributed to the owner class, same as bb_graph
tools.performance: maxNodes, maxLinks, scope, relationshipTypes, and languages constrain graph construction.
tools.safety: Read-only. HTML output contains the same bounded graph as JSON and does not mutate the project.
tools.evidence: Nodes and links resolve to canonical indexed entities; links with omitted endpoints are not emitted.

tools.name: bb_migrate
tools.description: Read-only single or batch migration planning with dependency order, explicit effort methodology, library mappings, risks, truncation, and unsupported cases. Plans whose source file changed since the last index are flagged stale up front — a plan is a claim about current code; JSON output carries the freshness block.

symbolNames.description: one or more symbols to migrate

documentation.summary: Batch cross-language migration plans with ordering, methodology, and unsupported mappings.

returns: Dependency-ordered migration plans
Effort methodology, library mappings, and risks
Explicit unsupported and truncation results
limitations: Plans are estimates, not translated source
Library mappings are advisory and unsupported routes remain explicit

Dependency ordering and mapping depend on the analyzer-extracted symbol and relationship graph; edge cases that the analyzers cannot resolve (reflection, dynamic dispatch, or cross-file relations the grammar does not model) limit the completeness of the resulting plan
tools.performance: Requests are capped at 100 symbols and dependency traversal is bounded.
tools.safety: Read-only. It does not generate, replace, or compile target-language source.
tools.evidence: Dependency ordering comes from indexed relationships; effort and mappings are labeled methodology-driven estimates.

tools.name: bb_analyze
tools.description: Unified evidence-backed analysis over graph relationships, dependencies, statistics, complexity, impact, and test intelligence. Select exactly one mode. Every read mode carries a freshness block (fresh/stale/missing counts + remediation) resolved against the live working tree; graph nodes and report rows carry a stale flag when their file changed after indexing. Callers/callees/trace/impact modes share the graph engine's owner-cascade semantics: a relationship stored against a class member is attributed to the owner class. Per-mode parameters: target applies to callers, callees, trace, complexity, impact, and test_impact; filePath scopes dependencies, test_mapping, test_gaps, and test_quality to a project-relative path prefix (others ignore it); stats is always project-wide.

target.description: symbol or analysis target (`symbol`/`symbolName`/`query` are accepted as aliases)

documentation.summary: One typed analysis surface replacing standalone relationship and test intelligence names.

returns: Mode-specific typed analysis
Graph, dependency, complexity, impact, or test evidence
Explicit unavailable and truncation states
errors: Missing target for a target-based mode
Option irrelevant to the selected mode
limitations: Static relationships cannot establish runtime behavior
Test results describe indexed static evidence, not executed coverage
Callers/callees/trace/impact modes share the graph engine's owner-cascade semantics: a relationship stored against a class member is attributed to the owner class

The callers/callees/trace modes bound each edge query by a declared per-symbol site limit (200) and report it in `summary.truncated` / `summary.truncationReason` with the root's true count in `summary.callersIfUncapped`; `summary.totalCallers` is the returned count, never a silent total (M59.A12, #888)
tools.performance: Mode-specific limits and graph traversal bounds prevent unbounded output.
tools.safety: Read-only. Analysis never creates tests or edits source.
tools.evidence: Findings derive from brain_* symbols, files, relationships, complexity, and test-file classifications.

tools.name: bb_doc
tools.description: Generate read-only, evidence-backed documentation with resolvable citations and a freshness block over the cited files. Supports symbol, file, module, feature, API, project, and documentation-coverage modes in Markdown or JSON.

target.description: symbol, file, module, feature, or API target (`symbol`/`symbolName`/`query` are accepted as aliases); optional for project and coverage

documentation.summary: Cited Markdown or JSON documentation over indexed source and relationships.

returns: Markdown or structured JSON documentation
Resolvable citations and evidence classifications
Quality and website reference metadata
limitations: Unknown facts remain explicit rather than inferred without support
Stale evidence is qualified and cannot silently become current
tools.performance: Evidence count and maxTokens impose explicit response budgets.
tools.safety: Read-only. It never refreshes implicitly, writes source, or invokes bb_edit.
tools.evidence: Claims are classified as extracted, inferred, generated, or unknown and carry resolvable citations where applicable.

tools.name: bb_edit
tools.description: Unified, validated source mutation. Discriminated by mode: write, update, insert, delete, or refactor. Supports dry-run previews, separator/symlink-safe paths, AST byte bounds, caller protection, rollback on validation failure, formatting, and reindexing. If the target file changed since it was indexed, this tool refreshes that one file and re-resolves the symbol before editing (reported in warnings) — an edit is never applied to stale byte bounds, and a symbol that was renamed or removed is refused by name.

mode.description: Edit kind: write (create or overwrite a file), update (replace a symbol body), insert (add code relative to a symbol), delete (remove a symbol), or refactor (identifier-aware rename)

dryRun.description: Preview the planned changes without writing any file (default false)

filePath.description: write: project-relative target file to create or overwrite. Other modes: disambiguates symbolName when it appears in multiple files

symbolName.description: Name of the symbol to update, delete, or refactor (the index must contain it; a target file changed since indexing is refreshed automatically before the edit)

lineStart.description: Declaration line of the target symbol, used with symbolName/filePath to disambiguate repeated names

content.description: Full file content for write mode; also accepted in place of newContent for update and insert

newContent.description: Replacement source: update swaps the symbol body for this text; insert adds this text relative to targetSymbolName

targetSymbolName.description: insert: symbol whose body or boundary receives the new code (required for insert)

position.description: insert anchor relative to targetSymbolName (default after)

newName.description: refactor: the valid identifier the symbol is renamed to

force.description: delete: allow removal when indexed callers or live references survive; leftovers are reported as warnings (default false)

format.description: Run the project formatter on written files after the edit (default true)

documentation.summary: Unified safe source editing with preview, validation, rollback, and reindex.

returns: Structured mutation result or dry-run preview
Validation, formatting, rollback, and reindex status
Affected paths and caller protection outcomes
errors: Ambiguous symbol name (the message names filePath/lineStart)
Symbol renamed or removed since the target file was indexed (refreshed first, then refused by name)
Caller protection, parse, formatting, or reindex failure
limitations: Named symbol edits need an INDEX, not a fresh one: when the target file changed after it was indexed, the tool refreshes that ONE file's rows and re-resolves the symbol before planning, so bounds always come from the bytes on disk and never from a stale span (M59.A11, #890). The refresh is reported in `warnings`; if the symbol was renamed or removed in the meantime the edit is refused by name instead of guessing a span

Directly after a write, the file's own evidence is current but cross-file relationships are only re-derived within the bounded post-pass, so a caller in an unrelated file may lag until the next dir index (same bound as bb_index)
Refactoring is identifier-aware static rewriting, not a full language-server proof

Per-mode argument rejection names the offending fields but not the accepted set for the mode (e.g. `bb_edit update mode does not accept: position` does not say that `update` accepts only `mode, dryRun, filePath, symbolName, lineStart, content/newContent, format`); callers must consult the mode contract in this page when constructing payloads. Known gap in `validateEditArguments` (src/mcp/tool-validation.ts). proof
tools.performance: Only affected files are written, formatted, validated, and reindexed.
tools.safety: Write-capable. Uses project-root path checks, atomic writes, snapshots, validation, and rollback; use dryRun before risky edits. dryRun writes no source file, but a stale target file is still refreshed in the INDEX first (derived data only), because the bounds it previews must be the bounds the real edit would use.
tools.evidence: Mutation bounds come from indexed AST bytes, re-resolved from the file on disk whenever the indexed rows are stale; validation and reindex state report whether post-edit evidence is current.

tools.name: bb_index
tools.description: Reindex a file or directory so the index reflects edits immediately (agent-fresh). Accepts a path (file or dir); a file reindexes only that file, a dir runs an incremental index of that dir (changed files only). mode=post re-runs the heavy derived-data phases (relationships/enrichment/gravity/taints/health) WITHOUT re-parsing — the remediation after edits on incremental paths. Returns indexed/deleted/error counts, or the per-phase post-processing report.

path.description: Project-relative file (reindex only that file) or directory (incremental index of changed files); for mode=post, the project whose derived phases should be re-run

mode.description: auto (default) infers file vs dir from path; file reindexes one file; dir runs an incremental directory index; post re-runs derived phases (relationships/taints/health) without re-parsing

documentation.summary: Immediately refresh the index for a just-written/edited file or directory; mode=post re-derives relationships/taints/health without re-parsing.

returns: Indexed, deleted, and error counts for the refreshed path
Mode actually applied (auto resolved, file, or dir)
Per-file error names for any file that failed to reindex
errors: Parse or store failure for an individual file
limitations: A file reindex updates only that file's evidence; cross-file relationships refresh on the next full or incremental dir index
Dir mode reuses the incremental indexer: unchanged files are skipped by design
tools.performance: A single file reindex is bounded by that file's parse cost; dir mode is bounded by the changed-file set.
tools.safety: Write-capable against index data only. It never modifies source files.
tools.evidence: Counts come from the real parse/store pipeline; errors name the file that failed rather than swallowing it.

tools.name: bb_graph
tools.description: Per-symbol dependency graph over the canonical graph engine: callers, callees, per-edge evidence tier (structural/import_based/usage_contextual/reference_qualified/inferred), confidence, and cross-language edge count. Same engine and tier rules the editor graph panel uses; truncated traversals are declared with a reason, never silent. Traversal semantics: a relationship stored against any member of a class (a method call, an inherited behavior) is attributed to the owner class, so caller/callee sets include the owner-family level — every edge still traces to a stored relationship row.

symbol.description: symbol name to root the graph at (`target`/`symbolName`/`query` are accepted as aliases)

direction.description: which side to traverse (default both). 'callers' answers "who depends on this" and skips the callee walk entirely — on a real index that is the difference between 1 edge and 37 in the same payload.

relationshipTypes.description: stored relationship kinds to include. Default: calls, instantiates, extends, implements. Pass e.g. ['calls'] for the pure call graph, or ['implements'] to see only interface satisfaction. A kind that is not listed is never reported, so this is how you exclude the type-level 'uses'/'references' rows that make up roughly half of what a typical index stores.

includeCrossLanguage.description: include edges the indexer marked cross-language (default true). Set false for a single-language view.

edgeLimit.description: Per-symbol call-site limit for one edge query (default 200, max 5000). Reaching it is declared in `summary.truncated` with `summary.truncationReason` and the root's true count in `summary.callersIfUncapped`/`summary.calleesIfUncapped` — the limit is never a silent cap. Raise it to receive more sites in one answer.

documentation.summary: Per-symbol graph with per-edge evidence tiers — the agent view of the editor's graph panel.

returns: Per-symbol dependency graph: callers and callees
Per-edge endpoints as described nodes — `{ id, name, symbolType, file, line, isExternal }` on BOTH ends, so an edge is self-contained and no id has to be parsed or looked up in a second call
Per-edge `rowId`: the stored `brain_relationship` row the edge came from, so every claim is auditable against the index (measured: every emitted rowId resolves to exactly one stored row)

Per-edge `match` (`exact` | `owner-cascade`) and `matchedMember` (`{ name, file }` when the cascade matched): whether the stored row names the symbol that was asked for, or one of its members folded onto it
Per-edge evidence tier (structural/import_based/usage_contextual/reference_qualified/inferred) with confidence

Per-edge call-site address (M62.A2): `{ kind, file, line, note }` — `call-site` is an exact stored line; `declaration` is a LABELED substitute (the calling symbol's own declaration, shown only when no call-site line is stored); `unknown` has no position at all (line null) and states why. A position is never fabricated and never reported as line 0
`summary.exactCallers` / `cascadedCallers` / `exactCallees` / `cascadedCallees`: how much of the answer is about the symbol that was asked for and how much the owner cascade folded in
`summary.edgesInBothDirections`: stored rows present in both the caller and the callee list — `totalCallers + totalCallees` double-counts exactly this many
`root.candidates`: how many stored symbols the requested name resolved among — 1 means the name was unique, more means the answer is about one of several and `root` is what to confirm

`summary.scope`: the `direction`, `relationshipTypes` and `includeCrossLanguage` actually applied, so a narrowed traversal returning zero edges is distinguishable from a widened one that found nothing
Declared truncation with a reason when the traversal is bounded
errors: relationshipTypes given as an empty list (a narrowed traversal that can match nothing is refused rather than silently returning an empty graph)
Symbol not found in the index
limitations: Edges reflect indexed static evidence with declared tiers; inferred edges are labeled, not proven
The graph reflects the index as of the last index run

Owner-cascade attribution: a relationship stored against a class member (e.g. a call to a method) is reported toward the owner class, so caller/callee sets are a superset of exact-symbol-only matches. The superset is REDUCIBLE: every edge carries `match` (`exact` or `owner-cascade`) and, when cascaded, `matchedMember` naming the member the stored row actually referenced, and the summary carries the exact/cascade split. Measured on cobra, `Command` (182 methods) answers with 184 caller edges of which 24 name `Command` itself — a ratio no per-edge field alone makes obvious, and one no count in the payload revealed before the split existed. Every edge also carries the `rowId` it traces to

A symbol name is not a unique identifier. When one name matches several stored symbols the resolver takes the highest-gravity match (ties broken by lowest id, so the pick is reproducible rather than SQLite's whim) and says how many it chose between in `root.candidates` — measured: `build` in lodash resolves among 7, `code_block.go` in cobra among 50, `Command` among 1. When `root.candidates` is greater than 1 the graph is about ONE of those symbols, so confirm `root` is the one you meant before reading the edges. The other candidates are not listed

A name containing a SQL LIKE wildcard (`%`, `_`) is matched LITERALLY, not as a pattern: it either resolves to a symbol that genuinely contains those characters or is reported not found. It never widens into a match on an unrelated symbol

Call-site positions depend on the analyzer: an exact line is claimed only where the index stored a real line; a legacy 0 or a NULL line yields the declared `declaration` or `unknown` address instead (derived by src/intelligence/graph/line-address.ts — never an inline fallback)

`summary.totalCallers`/`totalCallees` are the RETURNED counts, not the totals. A per-symbol site limit (`edgeLimit`, default 200, max 5000) bounds one edge query; when it is reached the answer declares `truncated` with `truncationReason` naming the bound (`caller-site-limit` / `callee-site-limit`), `cappedQueries` says how many queries hit it, and `callersIfUncapped`/`calleesIfUncapped` carry the root's true site count (null when no cap was reached — never zero). Before M59.A12 (#888) the limit was silent: a symbol with 3,437 call sites answered 200 rows with `truncated: false`. The cap now fires only when rows were ACTUALLY dropped: the query asks for one row beyond the limit, so a symbol holding exactly `edgeLimit` sites is reported complete instead of falsely truncated
tools.performance: maxDepth (default 3, max 10) bounds traversal; per-edge evidence resolution is bounded by the returned subgraph. `direction` halves the work when only one side is wanted — measured on cobra, a caller-only question about a symbol with 36 callees returned 1 edge instead of 37. The per-direction fan-out budget (50 symbols) is internal and is not exposed: truncation is declared in the summary when it bites.
tools.safety: Read-only. It does not modify source files or index data.
tools.evidence: Nodes and edges come from the canonical graph engine over brain_symbol and brain_relationship rows; each edge carries its evidence tier, its confidence, and the `rowId` of the row it came from. The declared totals are counted with the same query and the same noise filters as the returned edges, so a reported total is the number a caller would receive if no limit existed — verified against an independent SQL count on real repos (validation/m59/results/cap-real-corpus.json). Owner-cascade edges are auditable in the same way: `match` and `matchedMember` identify the member the stored row actually named, and the exact/cascade split in the summary is verified against an independent SQL count of direct-target rows on real repos (cobra: tool reports `exactCallers: 24`; oracle counts 24 direct caller rows for the same symbol).

tools.name: bb_impact
tools.description: Bounded reverse-dependency impact for one symbol via the same component the editor graph panel uses: declared node budget (200) and depth (5), truncation as a first-class field with reason, and an independently declared total when computable. Unknown symbols are loud declared errors — an empty impact set is never invented. Owner-cascade applies: impact includes dependents attributed at class level, not only exact-symbol rows.

symbol.description: symbol name to compute impact for (`target`/`symbolName`/`query` are accepted as aliases)

documentation.summary: Bounded impact with declared truncation — identical numbers to the editor's impact mode.

returns: Downstream dependents of the symbol with per-edge evidence tiers and confidence, cross-language flags, bridge mechanism, and each dependent's own position

How the requested name became the root it walked: `rootMatch` carries the name asked for, whether the match was exact, a containment match, or the member→owner substitution, and how many stored symbols carry that exact name

The declared limits, from the component that owns them: `budget` (node budget, depth, and the two ceilings the declared total is computed under) and `traversal` (depth actually reached, the engine's own truncation state and reason, its per-query site limit, its capped-query count, and the root's uncapped caller count when computable)

`directCount` — the exact number of DIRECT dependents, or `null` when the counting walk hit a declared ceiling. `totalCountIfKnown` is the true transitive total under the same rule, or `null` for a declared unknown. Neither is ever smaller than `shownCount`

Freshness: a per-dependent `stale` flag (`true`/`false`, or `null` when the file is not in the index at all) and a summary `freshness` envelope; `rootStale` declares the root's own file separately, since a stale root with fresh dependents is still a stale answer
Declared-absent result when the symbol is unknown — never an empty guess
errors: Symbol not found in the index
The named symbol exists but is not a traversable root (an enum member, a constant, a plain field) — a declared error naming the kind, never an empty set
limitations: Static impact analysis cannot establish runtime behavior
Reflects the index as of the last index run; the freshness envelope states how far that is from the files on disk
Owner-cascade attribution applies: dependents through class-member relationships are attributed to the owner class

A truncated answer is a bounded PREFIX of the set, not a sample of it: the walk is depth-first, so a hub's 200 returned rows are an exploration order, not the 200 nearest dependents. `directCount` is the field that makes the shape readable
tools.performance: Complete answers stay under ~250 ms on the lane's corpora. A truncated hub pays for an unbounded counting walk so the declared total is honest: 0.5–2.0 s, bounded by two declared ceilings (50 000 scanned rows, 2 000 expansions) past which the total is a declared `null` rather than a number paid for with seconds.
tools.safety: Read-only. It does not modify source files or index data.
tools.evidence: Impact derives from brain_relationship rows via the same engine the editor impact panel uses. The declared total is measured by an independent bounded walk under the traversal's own rule — same relationship kinds, same owner cascade, same noise policy, same depth — so it is the size of the set the answer is a prefix of, and an independent oracle in the bb_impact corpus lane checks both against the stored tables on nine real repositories.

tools.name: bb_cross_language
tools.description: Cross-language facts for one symbol from stored brain_relationship rows only (is_cross_language = 1), per-pair with bridge mechanism and evidence tier. Every fact names both ends: the copy of the requested name it came from, and the other symbol's name, file, language and line, plus the stored row id. A name is many symbols — the index holds one per (file, name, line) — so facts are the union over every copy, `copies` names them, and `ambiguous` says so; absence is declared only when no copy holds a stored row. The answer is bounded by `limit` (default 200, max 1000) with `truncated` and `totalCountIfKnown` declared. Pairs with no stored rows are declared absent — this tool never infers, guesses, or aspires. Same source and laws as the editor's cross-language hover section.

symbol.description: symbol name to fetch cross-language facts for (`target`/`symbolName`/`query` are accepted as aliases)

limit.description: max facts to return (default 200, max 1000); truncation is declared, never silent

documentation.summary: Stored cross-language pairs, each naming both ends, with declared absence and declared truncation.

returns: One fact per stored cross-language row touching the name, each naming BOTH ends — the copy of the requested name it came from (`self`: symbol, file, language, line) and the counterparty (`other`: symbol, file, language, line) — plus the stored `rowId`, the direction, the bridge, the evidence tier and the confidence

`copies`: every indexed symbol that carries the name, with its file, language, line and cross-row count, plus `ambiguous` and `ambiguityNote` when the index holds more than one (the index has one symbol per file/name/line, so a common name is many symbols)
Declared absent only when NO copy of the name holds a stored cross-language row, with the copy count in the note

Declared truncation: `truncated`, `truncationReason` and `totalCountIfKnown` when the `limit` bounded the answer; `unpairableRowCount` and `collapsedRowCount` report rows that could not name a pair and rows matched from both directions
errors: Symbol not found in the index (declared, not an empty set)
limit outside the declared 1..1000 range (refused, never clamped silently)
limitations: Reads stored is_cross_language=1 relationship rows only; never infers cross-language facts
Coverage depends on the analyzers that produced cross-language rows — this tool reports what was stored, nothing more
A name is many symbols: the answer is the UNION over every copy, never a silent choice among them. Narrow with the `copies` list — every fact names the copy it came from

`bridge` is the stored `bridge_mechanism`. On a real polyglot corpus it is almost always the indexer's `name-resolution` placeholder, which means two identifiers matched by name — not that the two languages communicate by that mechanism. Weigh it with `tier` and `confidence`
A row whose endpoint file has no detected language cannot name a pair; those rows are counted in `unpairableRowCount` and never dressed up with a guessed language
tools.performance: Two indexed queries (the stored cross-language rows for the name, and every symbol carrying the name), no graph traversal; the response is bounded by `limit` and declares what it dropped.
tools.safety: Read-only. It does not modify source files or index data.
tools.evidence: Only brain_relationship rows with is_cross_language=1, filtered by the row's own project_id, classified by the single evidence-tier rule in src/lsp/evidence_tier.ts — the same stored rows and the same rule as the editor cross-language hover section, over a projection that names both ends because a hover card already shows which file the reader is in and an agent does not. Every count is cross-checked against an independent SQL count over a real polyglot corpus (script/m63/verify-cl1-cross-language.ts, validation/m63/results/CL1.json).

tools.name: bb_annotate
tools.description: Attach an agent-authored annotation to a symbol in the shared index. Provenance is enforced: the row records author class 'agent' (never spoofable), the calling tool identity, and timestamps. Re-annotating the same symbol+path updates the note in place — one note per author per location. Annotations are opinions layered on evidence, never index facts, and surface in the editor where the human reads (hover + graph). To change source code use bb_edit; to read notes back use bb_annotations.

symbol.description: symbol name to annotate (`target`/`query` are accepted as aliases)

path.description: optional file path to disambiguate same-named symbols

toolIdentity.description: optional name of the calling agent/tool (recorded verbatim)

documentation.summary: Agent note with enforced provenance, stored where the human reads.

examples.body: Legacy auth path — scheduled for removal in Q3.

returns: Stored annotation id and provenance (tool identity, timestamp)
Declared refusals for a missing/blank symbol, an empty body, or an over-limit body
errors: Empty body (a refusal, not a silent no-op)
limitations: Annotations are opinions layered on index evidence, never index truth
Annotation store semantics are owned by the M28 workstream
Any symbol name is accepted; the note is not verified against the index, so a typo'd name is stored as given
tools.performance: Constant-time store write bounded by the 2000-char body limit.
tools.safety: Write-capable against the annotation store only. It never modifies source files.
tools.evidence: Annotations carry provenance (toolIdentity, time) and are stored in brain_annotation.

tools.name: bb_annotations
tools.description: Read annotations for a symbol (or all annotations up to the declared limit) with full provenance on every row: author class, tool identity, and timestamps. No annotations is a declared absence, never an error. To write a note use bb_annotate.

symbol.description: symbol name (omit to list all annotations); `target`/`query` are accepted as aliases

path.description: optional file path; returns that file's copy's notes plus any name-level notes (written with no path). Omit to return every note for the symbol

documentation.summary: Annotations with full provenance; absence declared.

returns: Typed annotations for a symbol or the whole project, with full provenance (author class, tool identity, timestamps)
Declared-absent result when none exist — absence is never an error
limitations: Reads only stored annotations; absence is declared, not inferred
Annotation store semantics are owned by the M28 workstream
Without `path`, a symbol that lives in several files returns every file's notes together; pass `path` (or read each row's symbol_path) to separate them
tools.performance: Indexed lookup by project and symbol (brain_annotation_project_symbol_idx).
tools.safety: Read-only. It does not modify source files, index data, or annotations.
tools.evidence: Rows come from brain_annotation with provenance fields preserved.
